messages.subject_clean: scale_fill_manual failed to show all colors
messages.body_plain:
King,

The factor used to identify your values is made in the ggplot2 call and does not contain the levels that you are assigning for the colors so those extra levels are ignored. Best to define these from the beginning and use them.

Data %>%
> mutate(value = lvls_expand(as.factor(value), as.character(0:6))) %>%
> ggplot(., aes(x=sample, y=gene)) +
> > geom_tile(aes(fill=value), colour = "black") +
> > scale_fill_manual(values = colvalue, drop=FALSE)
> >
> >
forcats::lvls_expand makes adding those levels pretty easy, but needs to be a character vector. You still need drop = FALSE in the scale_*_manual() call.

HTH,
B

Thanks,
Kevin

I don't know. I would take the approach of setting them manually, which has the added advantage of letting you chose your colour scheme. Add a call to scale_fill_manual and scale_colour_manual with a vector of colours.

I think the fill in your aesthetic (and consequently a call to scale_fill_manual) might be irrelevant as most shapes don't have a fill attribute, only a colour one. I'd check this but I don't have my PC to hand.

Alternatively, the default list of colours is available online at
http://www.cookbook-r.com/Graphs/Colors_(ggplot2)/
Although if you plan to do something like refer to a feature of your graph via something like 'the blue point in figure 1' you might find the default colours a challenge to describe/name. I do.

Regards,
Ron.

My x axis uses a custom transformation, and when I do a single plot everything looks fine.  But when I use facet, the only label on the x axis is 0 at the far left.

Secondly, I'm only using the transformation so that my values of 30, 90, and 180 appear equal distances apart.  This seems like a very elaborate way to do that.  Is there an alternative?  Usually I would just make day (the x-axis variable) a factor, but in this case if I do so I get an error that every group has only 1 point.

Code follows.  The goal, within each facet, is to plot a bunch of paths, one for each F_PID.  Each path has at most 3 points in it.
 tvforward <- function(x) {
    x <- x / 30 - 1  # values are now 0, 2, 5
    x <- 1 + pmin(x, 2) / 2 + pmax(x - 3, 0) / 2
  }
  tvinv <- function(v) {
    # the plot machinery generates v outside the range we picked
  -30 + 60 * v + 30 * pmax(v - 2, 0)
  }
  visit_trans <- function() {
    trans_new("visit", transform = tvforward,
              inverse = tvinv)
  }
  g <- ggplot(plotdat, aes(x = day, y = GOSE, color = F_PID)) +
    geom_line(position = position_jitter(width = 0.1, height = 0.3), size =
                1) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      breaks = 2:8,
      minor_breaks = NULL,
      limits = c(1.5, 8.5)
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      trans = visit_trans(),
      breaks = c(30, 90, 180),
      minor_breaks = NULL
    ) + facet_wrap(~group )+
    guides(colour="none")+
    ggtitle("Sample Histories for Each Group", "Only those observed at 180 days")
  plot(g)
